beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A formal proof checker rejects invalid proofs within its own stated assumptions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A physical experiment also depends on instruments, calibration and a model of measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Social inquiry introduces further questions about categories, values and whose experience is absent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book preserves a common architecture without pretending these evaluators are interchangeable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Delegation should therefore depend on the domain and the consequences of failure.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chapter seven develops those contrasts beyond the familiar demonstration of a coding agent.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Human governance means more than clicking approval after the important choices are already made.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: People must be able to shape purposes, inspect assumptions and stop consequential actions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A right of appeal needs an authority capable of changing the outcome.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Infrastructure ownership and access also affect whose criticism can receive a hearing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book treats these as scientific design questions, not administrative additions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its research programme asks how automation can preserve responsible delegation without ceremonial oversight.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That is one reason the volume connects technical systems to a republic of knowledge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Every validator and provenance requirement consumes time, computation or scarce expert attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book does not argue that maximum infrastructure always produces better science.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A simpler system may be preferable if it corrects a bounded failure effectively.
